title: Common-degree twists are invertible on a quasi-compact Proj open
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and let $U\subseteq P$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose homogeneous elements $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of positive degrees cover $U$ by $U\subseteq\bigcup_iD_+(f_i)$. If $e\geq1$ is a common multiple of their degrees, let $W_e$ be the largest open subscheme of $P$ on which every $\mathcal O_P(ne)$ is invertible and all multiplication maps $\mathcal O_P(ne)\otimes\mathcal O_P(me)\to\mathcal O_P((n+m)e)$ are isomorphisms (equivalently, the union of standard opens $D_+(ab)$ with homogeneous $a,b$ and $\deg(a)=\deg(b)+e$). Then $U\subseteq W_e$; consequently, for every $k\geq1$, the restricted twist $\mathcal O_U(ek)=\mathcal O_P(ek)|_U$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], and the canonical multiplication map $\mathcal O_U(e)^{\otimes k}\to\mathcal O_U(ek)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj), proof after the finite standard-open cover: clauses (1)--(4), using Tag 01MS (lemma-where-invertible).

proof.text: Because U is quasi-compact and the positive-degree standard opens form a basis of Proj(A), the assumed cover has a finite subcover; after reindexing, we may use the given finite list f_1, ..., f_r. The quasi-compactness definition is exactly the finite-subcover property, and the standard-open result supplies the positive-degree basis.

source.place: Tag 01MW proof, first sentence; Tag 01M4 and Algebra Tag 00JP for the positive-degree standard-open basis.

proof.text: Let d_i=deg(f_i) and choose the positive common multiple e from the hypothesis. For each i put g_i=f_i^{e/d_i}; then deg(g_i)=e and D_+(g_i)=D_+(f_i), since a homogeneous prime contains f_i exactly when it contains a positive power of f_i. Thus the D_+(g_i) still cover U. This is the elementary common-degree replacement in the proof of Tag 01MW.

source.place: Tag 01MW proof, first paragraph: d=d_1...d_n and D_+(f_i)=D_+(f_i^{d/d_i}).

proof.text: The invertibility-locus characterization says that W_e is the union of standard opens D_+(ab) with homogeneous a,b satisfying deg(a)=deg(b)+e. Taking a=g_i and b=1 gives D_+(g_i)=D_+(g_i\cdot1) contained in W_e for every i. Hence U, covered by these opens, is contained in W_e.

source.place: Tag 01MS (lemma-where-invertible), characterization (2), applied in Tag 01MW proof.

proof.text: By the definition of W_e, on U every O_U(ne)=O_P(ne)|_U is invertible and every multiplication map O_U(ne) tensor O_U(me) -> O_U((n+m)e) is an isomorphism. In particular O_U(ek) is invertible for k>=1.

source.place: Tag 01MS characterization (1), restricted from W_e to U.

proof.text: Compose the multiplication isomorphism for (e,(k-1)e) with the inductively obtained identification O_U(e)^{tensor (k-1)} ≅ O_U((k-1)e), starting from k=1. Associativity of tensor products makes this the canonical map O_U(e)^{tensor k} -> O_U(ek), and it is an isomorphism for every k>=1.

source.place: Tag 01MW clauses (1)--(4), using the multiplication maps from Tag 01MS.
